obtained.how: agency copy: Michigan DNR Fisheries Division research report library (PDF with a text layer, 15 pages)

bibliography.note: Michigan Department of Natural Resources, Fisheries Division, Fisheries Research Report No. 1792, May 16, 1973; "The fish population of Cassidy Lake, Washtenaw County" by James C. Schneider (Dingell-Johnson Project F-29-R). "Ann Arbor" is not on the title page.

claims.claim: Cassidy Lake, Michigan: 18.6 ha, max 3.4 m, weedy, hard water
claims.quote: shallow (maximum depth of 11 feet), weedy, has hard water
claims.conditions: 46 acres = 18.6 ha; 11 ft = 3.35 m; methyl orange alkalinity 134 ppm

claims.claim: method: mark–recapture checked by rotenone; fish ≥ 7.6 cm
claims.source_value: fish marked in trap nets (8–18 May 1964) and a seine (21–28 May) and recaptured by seining or in the sample of dead fish picked up 1–3 June after the rotenone treatment of 1 June: the rotenone pick-up was a RECAPTURE sample, not a total count; Schumacher-Eschmeyer or Bailey-Petersen estimates, stratified by inch group, with the minimum known number or "a conservative approximation" substituted where data were short. The ≥ 3.0-in (7.6-cm) limit applies to the bluegill, pumpkinseed, yellow perch and largemouth bass estimates only; no size limit is given for the other species' counts
claims.quote: Additional estimates were made when the lake was subsequently treated with rotenone
claims.note: write "mark–recapture, with recaptures at a rotenone treatment"; the lake was poisoned, but the dead fish were sampled, not counted

claims.quote: The total standing crop of fish was about 145 pounds per acre.
claims.conditions: p. 7 calls it "the total standing crop of fish of all sizes"; May 1964
claims.note: 145 lb/acre × 1.1209 = 162.5 kg/ha. The biomass is for all sizes (p. 7), while the row's "fish ≥ 7.6 cm" fits only the four main species' numbers

claims.location: p. 4 (PDF p. 4) other species; p. 10 (PDF p. 10), Table 3
claims.conditions: sum of the Table 3 age-group estimates for bluegill, pumpkinseed, perch and largemouth (≥ 3.0 in) plus the p. 4 counts of nine other species (no size limit stated)
claims.note: Table 3 sums (bluegill 52,054; pumpkinseed 7,875; perch 33,996; bass 713) + other species 7,072 (125 crappie, 30 rock bass, 3,400 green sunfish, 1,730 yellow bullhead, 900 brown/black bullhead, 450 lake chubsucker, 81 large bowfin, 356 grass pickerel) = 101,710 / 18.62 ha = 5,464/ha ≈ 5,470. Table 2 (inch-group strata, which the text calls the best estimates) gives perch 33,063 and bass 779, total 100,843 = 5,417/ha. Either rounds to ~5,400–5,500/ha; read on the page images

claims.location: p. 4 (PDF p. 4); p. 10 (PDF p. 10), Table 3; p. 9, Table 2
claims.quote: 14. 5 for the pumpkinseed, 23. 5 for the yellow perch

claims.claim: only ≈ 10 perch/ha > 17.8 cm, about a 180-fold drop from the ≥ 7.6-cm count
claims.quote: there were only about 4 perch per acre larger than 7. 0 inches
claims.conditions: "In Cassidy and Mill lakes, for example" — the figure is given for both lakes together

claims.note: 7,875 / 18.62 ha = 423/ha (Table 2 and Table 3 agree); 14.5 lb/acre = 16.3 kg/ha

claims.claim: brown and black bullhead 48/ha (14 kg/ha); grass pickerel 19/ha
claims.quote: 900 brown and black bullheads (Ictalurus nebulosus and I. melas) weighing 12. 5 pounds
claims.conditions: no size limit stated for these species' counts

claims.claim: in unfished Mill Lake, Michigan, which held largemouth and pike, yellow perch lost 70 % a year, all from natural causes
claims.location: p. 6 (PDF p. 6), Discussion; p. 6–7 for the closure and predators
claims.quote: Total annual mortality was high in both lakes: 80-96% in Cassidy and 70% in Mill.
claims.conditions: Mill Lake closed to fishing ("where angling was prohibited"); northern pike 2–9 lb/acre in Sugarloaf and Mill, largemouth 12 lb/acre in Mill; total mortality from age-frequency (catch-curve) estimates under roughly constant recruitment; the Discussion compares Cassidy with Mill Lake as described by Schneider (1971), which is presumably where the Mill figures come from
claims.note: "All from natural causes" follows from the closure: Schneider states it outright for Mill Lake pumpkinseed ("because the lake was closed to fishing") and bluegill. No size threshold is given for the Mill perch rate in this report

claims.claim: pumpkinseed total annual mortality A in the 68–72 % range (Schneider 1973a; Snow 1978)
claims.quote: Total mortality for the pumpkinseed was about 68% per year
claims.conditions: Cassidy Lake, May 1964, catch curve over age groups II–VI; includes fishing (amount unknown)
claims.note: Schneider's 68 % is the Cassidy value. For large pumpkinseed he also gives 81 % at Sugarloaf (29 % fishing, 52 % natural) and 57 % at Mill (all natural, closed to fishing): the three Waterloo lakes span 57–81 %

notes: Only the method wording in Table 3.5-1 needs changing (rotenone was a recapture sample). The density figures use Table 3's age-group sums; Table 2's inch-group sums are ~1–3 % lower. Other values here: Cassidy yellow perch total mortality 80–96 % a year (angling likely), bluegill 63 %, largemouth 26 % (age II) to 73 % (age VIII); Mill bluegill ≥ 6 in 54 %, legal bass 41 % (all natural); Sugarloaf large bluegill 66 % (25 % fishing). Total standing crops: Sugarloaf 95, Mill 116, Cassidy 145 lb/acre.
